correctness.rationale: The two-step formulas follow from independent per-white-vertex binomial success probabilities and cover the j=0 boundary correctly. The comparison uses strict central-binomial lower bounds for even b>=14 and odd b>=17, with exact positive D_b for b=3,...,15; script independently checks all finite constants and labeled-vertex dynamics. The late-time statement follows from initial self-loop probabilities lambda_A=(1-1/b)^b and lambda_B=1/4, all reachable later states having self-loop <1/4, finite triangular transient matrices, and a geometric first-exit decomposition yielding positive finite asymptotic constants. No finite experiment is used to infer the infinite result.

value.rationale: The seed-placement question is directly motivated by a published conjecture comparing expected completion times on complete bipartite graphs. The new result gives an all-size (not isolated finite) horizon-dependent reversal, with a strict two-round optimization in one direction and an exact opposite late-time exponential rate. This prevents strengthening the expected-time preference to first-order stochastic dominance and distinguishes quantile/reliability decisions from mean-based seed selection. The central-binomial and state-spectrum arguments are substantive and do not reduce to a tiny normalisation or naming change.
